meta.title: Tax-Advantaged Accounts
meta.description: A visual guide to tax-advantaged accounts — 401(k), 403(b), Roth IRA, Roth 401(k), HSA, FSAs, 529, Coverdell ESA, SEP IRA, solo 401(k), executive bonus plans, and IUL — organized by who they fit, with 2026 IRS limits and worked examples.
meta.note: The collection hub at /blogs/tax-advantaged-accounts.html is hand-built (meta.customHub). Do not point tools/build_blog_hubs.py at that file. Optional meta.tagPages entries turn matching tag pills into links; customPage skips overwriting the hub.

tagPages.label: Tax-Advantaged Accounts
tagPages.description: Tax-advantaged accounts organized by who they fit, with 2026 IRS limits, catch-up rules, and worked examples.

posts.title: Diane Still Thought of It as the Company Plan
posts.desc: A fictional 52-year-old employee walks through 2026 401(k) and 403(b) deferral limits, catch-up contributions, and why traditional workplace plans are tax-deferred — not tax-free.
posts.imageAlt: An empty workplace desk with a sage blotter, a plant, and a window looking onto trees

posts.title: Nina Kept Waiting for the Perfect Year to Open a Roth IRA
posts.desc: A fictional 47-year-old checks 2026 Roth IRA limits, income phase-outs, and the difference between tax-free qualified withdrawals and a deductible IRA.
posts.imageAlt: An open notebook and a cup of tea on a table against a sage wall

posts.title: Mark's HSA Clock Started Ticking at 55
posts.desc: A fictional 55-year-old on a high-deductible plan uses 2026 HSA limits, the age-55 catch-up, and the rule that Medicare enrollment stops contributions.
posts.imageAlt: An olive first-aid tin, glasses, a cream envelope, and eucalyptus on sage linen

posts.title: Priya's Catch-Up Had to Be Roth
posts.desc: A fictional 61-year-old uses the 2026 super catch-up, the Roth catch-up wage rule, and the fact that designated Roth 401(k) accounts have had no lifetime RMDs since 2024.
posts.imageAlt: Two cream envelopes on a sage table runner

posts.title: Elena's Three Envelopes
posts.desc: A fictional 46-year-old compares a 2026 health FSA, a limited-purpose FSA paired with an HSA, and a dependent care FSA — pre-tax accounts that are not tax-free in the Roth sense.
posts.imageAlt: A blank wall calendar, a sage mug, a stack of cream papers, and a bowl of green apples on a sunlit table

posts.title: Carol Opened a 529 for a Grandchild She Hadn't Met Yet
posts.desc: A fictional 58-year-old grandparent walks through 529 qualified withdrawals, the $20,000 K-12 cap after 2025, expanded uses, and the 529-to-Roth rollover rules.
posts.imageAlt: A wooden bench on a quiet autumn campus path beneath green and gold trees, with a brick building in the background

posts.title: James Thought a Coverdell Was Just a Smaller 529
posts.desc: A fictional 49-year-old parent compares a Coverdell ESA's $2,000 cap and income limits with a 529, using official IRS rules.
posts.imageAlt: A child's wooden desk with a stack of plain hardcover books, a green pencil cup, and a glass jar of coins

posts.title: Rob's Business Had No Employees. His Retirement Plan Did the Work.
posts.desc: A fictional 51-year-old self-employed owner compares 2026 SEP IRA and solo 401(k) limits, including catch-up contributions and the annual-additions cap.
posts.imageAlt: A wooden desk against a sage wall, with a closed cream notebook, a lamp, and a potted fig tree by a window

posts.title: Andrea's Bonus Came With a Life Insurance Policy
posts.desc: A fictional 54-year-old executive examines how a Section 162 executive bonus plan is taxed, what a double bonus covers, and why qualified accounts should be maxed first.
posts.imageAlt: An empty sage-leather chair at a walnut desk, with a green glass paperweight and a blank cream folder

posts.title: Walter Was Pitched an IUL as a Tax-Free Retirement Plan
posts.desc: A fictional 59-year-old reviews how indexed universal life actually works — caps, loans, MEC rules, and lapse risk — and what to max out before considering one.
posts.imageAlt: A closed cream folder, a calculator with a dark screen, and reading glasses on a sage linen runner
